section13_checks.prohibition_description: Treating Grant Agreement Annex templates as the governing structural schema for proposal writing.
section13_checks.violation_evidence: The artifact references application-form Part B anchors (B.1.1, B.1.2, B.2.1, B.2.2, B.3.1, B.3.2) and section tables (3.1a, 3.1b, 3.1d, 3.1f). These are Tier 2A application-form structures, not Grant Agreement Annexes. No string identifying a Grant Agreement Annex, Model Grant Agreement Annex, or AGA template is used as a structural authority.

section13_checks.prohibition_description: Inventing call constraints, scope requirements, expected outcomes, or expected impacts not present in Tier 2B source documents.
section13_checks.violation_evidence: The artifact references an established 'composition condition' and the 'lump-sum topic' as known call facts within deferred revision recommendations; it does not assert new or fabricated call constraints, scope boundaries, or expected impacts. The artifact is a review/status log, not a vehicle for call-requirement claims. No invented call constraint found.

section13_checks.prohibition_description: Inventing project facts (partners, capabilities, roles, objectives, prior experience, budget figures, team sizes, equipment) not present in Tier 3.
section13_checks.violation_evidence: The artifact does the opposite of fabrication: it explicitly declares project facts as absent or assumed and defers actions on that basis, citing §13.3. It records that 'all twelve partners are operator assumptions and P07-P12 are fictional gap partners', marks person-months 'not agreed'/'TBD', the 48-month duration 'assumed', and refuses to confirm beneficiaries or add a gender-of-research partner because those are 'new project fact[s] absent from Tier 3'. No project fact is asserted as confirmed.

section13_checks.prohibition_description: Commencing any Phase 8 activity before the budget gate (Phase 7) has passed.
section13_checks.violation_evidence: Audited artifact is a Phase 8 artifact (schema_id 'orch.phase8.drafting_review_status.v1'). Direct inspection of docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/budget_gate_assessment.json is outside the TAPM input boundary (reads limited to CLAUDE.md and artifact_path). Assessment therefore rests on the artifact's internal state: it treats cost-bearing effort as 'set against the externally validated budget (§13.4)' and 'the externally validated lump-sum budget', showing budget-gate awareness; and it contains no confirmed budget figures (person-months marked 'not agreed'/'TBD', duration marked 'assumed'). No budget-dependent content is finalized. No violation evidence found within the audited artifact.

section13_checks.prohibition_description: Storing durable decisions only in agent memory without writing them to Tier 4.
section13_checks.violation_evidence: Not checkable from artifact content alone; enforced by the decision-log-update skill. Non-applicable to artifact-level inspection. Recorded pass per skill specification. (Observationally, the artifact itself is a durable Tier 4 phase output recording revision dispositions, consistent with §13.5 rather than contrary to it.)

section13_checks.prohibition_description: Allowing a workflow or skill to become a de facto constitutional authority by expanding its scope to redefine phase, tier, or gate meanings.
section13_checks.violation_evidence: Not directly checkable from an artifact. Non-applicable to artifact-level inspection. Recorded pass per skill specification.

section13_checks.prohibition_description: Silently reordering phases or weakening gate conditions to allow workflow progress when inputs are incomplete.
section13_checks.violation_evidence: This is a Phase 8 artifact. It references only upstream inputs (Phase 7 budget, duration, consortium) and does not reference activities from any phase higher than its own. It declares incomplete inputs as unresolved and defers them to an operator-directed revision cycle rather than papering over gaps. No phase reordering or gate weakening present.

section13_checks.prohibition_description: Finalizing proposal text when source state is known to be incomplete, contradictory, or unvalidated, without explicitly flagging the gap in the deliverable.
section13_checks.violation_evidence: The artifact's own reasons state that each unresolved item is explicitly flagged within the section prose: B.1.1 'states Target numbers are not yet fixed'; Tables 3.1a/3.1b/3.1f 'mark every person-month cell not agreed/TBD'; Tables 3.1a/3.1d mark months 'not stated'; B.3.2 'flags the gap'. The gaps are surfaced in-content, satisfying §13.8. Note: direct verification of the Tier 5 section prose is outside the TAPM input boundary. A residual metadata tension exists — section_completion_log marks excellence and impact 'final' and implementation 'reviewed' with data_gaps_flagged:false, while nine of ten revision_actions (including criticals A-1 and A-2) remain unresolved — but this does not meet the §13.8 violation criterion, which requires unresolved content to be NOT flagged in the section content; per the artifact's representations, the content does flag it.

section13_checks.prohibition_description: Using agent-local knowledge of Horizon Europe programme rules as a substitute for reading Tier 1 source documents when those documents are present.
section13_checks.violation_evidence: The artifact makes no Tier 1 regulatory claim (participation conditions, grant agreement terms, financial regulation) asserted from generic programme knowledge. Its references to the 'composition condition' and the 'lump-sum topic' are call/eligibility matters, and its constitutional citations (§13.3, §13.4) point to CLAUDE.md, which is appropriate for a Tier 4 status artifact. No ungrounded regulatory claim found.
